questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,-1\le y<0\}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<2,\,\bbox[5px,border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14147181/assets/fc71859cb4d1e58ea3d15c2da66bce014898281fe237f2e0c2396f96c84c9e79.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14147181/assets/eff037b96b6a42120fdfa112a98d1e0749cdd56bd89acd647db448b08d7323ad.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,0<x<2,\,-1<y<0\,\}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,1<{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ contains none of its boundary points.

II. $A$ contains some (not all) of its boundary points.

III. $\text{int}\,A=A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14147181/assets/8414de2e05da43c03fae3c8b1ff2102401e990188e9fd4ee59a24308ec34b086.png)

 

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

Notice that, in this case, the set $A$ contains some (not all) of its boundary points.

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. As we have seen, $∂A$ consists of two concentric circles: the outer one is in $A,$ while the inner one is not.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ contains some of its boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\ne A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4y>{x}^{2}\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅$

II. $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A$

III. $∂A⊂A$
questions.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14147181/assets/a380742f47d97062d56b482592cd2d2961dcc40262131a99886b815c507ab6e3.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14147181/assets/26d264d702368ed6fe05577d7c34630bd16b41bdba8d206dd4db39763db02938.png)

 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cap ∂A=∅,$ where $∅$ denotes the empty set.

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $A-∂A=\text{int}\,A.$

- Statement III is false. In this case, the set $A$ contains none of its boundary points, so we must have $∂A⊈A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and  II only."
